objective.statement: Split the god-module checkout handler in src/handler.js into smaller modules as a pure refactor.
objective.success_definition: src/handler.js is decomposed into smaller modules, every public export is preserved, every existing test remains green, and there is zero behavior change — including leaving the known tax computation rounding discrepancy untouched.

goals.statement: Split the god-module checkout handler in src/handler.js into smaller modules.
acceptance: The checkout handler logic formerly in the god-module src/handler.js is decomposed into smaller modules.
All existing tests pass and every public export is preserved after the split.

goals.statement: Keep every public export of the checkout handler.
acceptance: Every public export that existed before the refactor is still exported after the refactor.
The entire existing test suite passes after the refactor.

goals.statement: Preserve behavior exactly — a pure refactor with zero behavior change.
acceptance: No observable behavior change results from the refactor; changes are limited to code motion and restructuring.

constraints.statement: Zero behavior change: the refactor must be pure, with no functional modifications.
Every public export must be kept.
Every existing test must remain green.
Do not fix the known rounding discrepancy in tax computation; it is explicitly out of scope for this refactor.

non_goals.statement: Fixing the known rounding discrepancy in tax computation.

assumptions.statement: The specific decomposition boundaries (which smaller modules to create and how responsibilities are divided among them) are left to the implementer, since the task does not prescribe a target module structure.
The existing test suite is currently green before the refactor begins, so 'keep every existing test green' means preserving an already-passing state.

open_questions.question: What target module structure is desired for the split (e.g., split by concern such as pricing, tax, payment, fulfillment), and should src/handler.js remain as a thin re-export facade to preserve public exports?
options: Implementer chooses a sensible decomposition by concern
Keep src/handler.js as a facade that re-exports from the new modules
Request a specific module layout from the requester before starting

verification.spec: Run the existing test suite after the refactor.
Compare the set of public exports before and after the refactor.
verification.expected: Every public export present before the refactor is still exported afterward.

verification.spec: Review the diff to confirm changes are limited to code motion and restructuring, and that the tax computation rounding logic is unchanged.
verification.expected: No functional modifications; the known rounding discrepancy remains exactly as before.

deliverables.description: The checkout handler in src/handler.js decomposed into smaller modules with all public exports preserved and no behavior change.

factors: Splitting a god-module touches many code paths, creating risk of accidental behavior change despite the pure-refactor requirement.
Public export surface must be preserved exactly; missed or renamed exports would break consumers.
Existing tests may not cover all behavior, so zero-behavior-change may not be fully verifiable by the test suite alone.
